7832	@@ -0,0 +1,123 @@
7833	+#!/usr/bin/env bats
7834	+# =============================================================================
7835	+# tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.3 (PRD FR-7 AC-7.5, SDD D-7.4, D-7.6).
7836	+#
7837	+# The dissent budget pre-check prices every planned voice — the primary, the companion's first hop, each advisory voice —
7838	+# at its catalog price (python3 -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias), instead of the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok.
7839	+# An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 for that voice and is said by name; a zero-priced entry estimates
7840	+# zero and is said too. Prices come from fixture entries in the test's project config (hounfour.providers overlays the
7841	+# catalog, as cheval merges it). Each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 × output rate, micro-USD/Mtok → cents.
7842	+# =============================================================================
7843	+
7844	+load adversarial-review-s3-helpers
7845	+
7846	+setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3bud; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
7847	+teardown() { s3_teardown; }
7848	+
7849	+_cfg() {  # <model> <budget> <companion_voice> [extra code_review lines]
7850	+    s3_config "hounfour:
7851	+  providers:
7852	+    openai:
7853	+      models:
7854	+        fixture-priced:
7855	+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 2000000, output_per_mtok: 8000000}
7856	+    fixturelocal:
7857	+      models:
7858	+        fixture-zero:
7859	+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0}
7860	+        fixture-stale:
7861	+          price_date: \"2000-01-01\"
7862	+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 1000000, output_per_mtok: 1000000}
7863	+flatline_protocol:
7864	+  code_review:
7865	+    enabled: true
7866	+    model: $1
7867	+    budget_cents: $2
7868	+    timeout_seconds: 30
7869	+    companion_voice: $3
7870	+    fallback_chain: []
7871	+${4:-}"
7872	+}
7873	+
7874	+_big_diff() {  # a diff whose estimate is 1,000,500 input tokens (3,000,000 bytes / 3 + 500)
7875	+    { printf 'diff --git a/x.sh b/x.sh\n'; head -c $(( 3000000 - 25 )) /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a'; } > "$T/diff.patch"
7876	+    [ "$(wc -c < "$T/diff.patch")" -eq 3000000 ]
7877	+}
7878	+
7879	+@test "BUD-1 the primary is priced at its catalog rate (no fixed-rate fallback): 1,000,500 tokens × 2 + 2000 × 8 USD/Mtok = 201c" {
7880	+    _big_diff
7881	+    _cfg fixture-priced 150 false
7882	+    result=$(s3_run review)
7883	+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
7884	+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.status' <<<"$result")" = "budget_exceeded" ]
7885	+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "201" ]
7886	+    [ "$(jq -c '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | {role, alias, estimated_cents, pricing_source}]' <<<"$result")" = '[{"role":"primary","alias":"fixture-priced","estimated_cents":201,"pricing_source":"config"}]' ]
7887	+    grep -qF "budget: estimate 201c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-priced 201c)" "$T/stderr.log"
7888	+    ! grep -q "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "a catalog-priced primary fell back"; return 1; }
7889	+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
7890	+}
7891	+
7892	+@test "BUD-2 an alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok for that voice, said by name (1000c + 6c)" {
7893	+    _big_diff
7894	+    _cfg mystery-model-x 150 false
7895	+    result=$(s3_run review)
7896	+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
7897	+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
7898	+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.estimate_voices[0].pricing_source' <<<"$result")" = "fallback" ]
7899	+    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (primary) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice" "$T/stderr.log"
7900	+    [ "$(grep -c "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log")" = "1" ]
7901	+}
7902	+
7903	+@test "BUD-3 a zero-priced entry estimates 0c and is said: a 0-cent budget admits it, where the fixed rate would refuse" {
7904	+    _cfg fixture-zero 0 false
7905	+    s3_run review >/dev/null
7906	+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
7907	+    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (primary) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
7908	+    grep -qF "budget: estimate 0c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-zero 0c)" "$T/stderr.log"
7909	+    grep -qx "fixture-zero" "$CALLS"
7910	+    # the same run priced at the fixed rate is refused (the regression this replaces: 2000 output tokens × 30 = 6c > 0)
7911	+    _cfg mystery-model-x 0 false
7912	+    s3_run review >/dev/null
7913	+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
7914	+}
7915	+
7916	+@test "BUD-4 the gate sums every planned voice: primary + the companion's first hop + each advisory voice" {
7917	+    _big_diff
7918	+    _cfg fixture-priced 1 true "    advisory_voices: [fixture-zero, mystery-model-x]"
7919	+    result=$(s3_run review)
7920	+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
7921	+    [ "$(jq -r '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | "\(.role)=\(.alias)"] | join(" ")' <<<"$result")" = "primary=fixture-priced companion=claude-headless advisory=fixture-zero advisory=mystery-model-x" ]
7922	+    # the companion's price is the catalog's (whatever it is today): recompute it from the same CLI
7923	+    local row ci co comp
7924	+    row=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias claude-headless --config "$CONFIG_FILE")
7925	+    ci=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$row"); co=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$row")
7926	+    [[ "$ci" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$co" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
7927	+    comp=$(( 1000500 * ci / 10000000000 + 2000 * co / 10000000000 ))
7928	+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[1].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "$comp" ]
7929	+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[2].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "0" ]
7930	+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[3].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
7931	+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "$(( 201 + comp + 0 + 1006 ))" ]
7932	+    [ "$(jq '[.metadata.estimate_voices[].estimated_cents] | add' <<<"$result")" = "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" ]
7933	+    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (advisory) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
7934	+    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (advisory)" "$T/stderr.log"
7935	+}

7938	+    _cfg fixture-stale 1000 false
7939	+    s3_run review >/dev/null
7940	+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
7941	+    grep -qF "budget: fixture-stale (primary) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given" "$T/stderr.log"
7942	+}
7943	+
7944	+@test "BUD-6 with no price CLI answer at all every voice falls back and is said (the gate never prices from nothing)" {
7945	+    _cfg fixture-priced 1000 false
7946	+    # a PYTHONPATH that cannot import the package: the CLI fails, every planned voice is unknown
7947	+    local real patched
7948	+    real="$(declare -f _adv_budget_estimate)"
7949	+    patched="${real/PYTHONPATH=\"\$PROJECT_ROOT\/.claude\/adapters\"/PYTHONPATH=/nonexistent}"
7950	+    [ "$patched" != "$real" ]   # (the seam was found: the CLI really cannot be imported in this run)
7951	+    eval "$patched"
7952	+    s3_run review >/dev/null
7953	+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ]
7954	+    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for fixture-priced (primary)" "$T/stderr.log"
7955	+}

1	# Multi-Model Activation Reference (cheval substrate)
2	
3	Full migration state, rollback model, and verification history for the cheval Python substrate. Moved out of `CLAUDE.loa.md`; the per-turn rules live there in compressed form.
4	
5	## Multi-Model Activation (cycle-109 sprint-3)
6	
7	The cheval Python substrate is the **unconditional** dispatch path for all
8	multi-model consumers (BB, Flatline orchestrator, Red-team pipeline,
9	adversarial-review, bridgebuilder-review, flatline-readiness,
10	red-team-model-adapter, post-pr-triage). The pre-cycle-109
11	`hounfour.flatline_routing` runtime flag is being phased out across the
12	T3.6→T3.7→T3.8 sequence.
13	
14	| Status (cycle-109 sprint-3 state) | BB | Flatline | Red-team |
15	|---|---|---:|---:|
16	| **Post-T3.6 (commit C — current)** | cheval (unchanged) | cheval (unconditional) | cheval (unconditional) |
17	| **Post-T3.7 (commit D — gated by C109.OP-S3)** | cheval | cheval | cheval (legacy file DELETED) |
18	| **Post-T3.8 (commit E)** | cheval | cheval | cheval (`hounfour.flatline_routing` flag REMOVED) |
19	
20	BB has used `ChevalDelegateAdapter` unconditionally since cycle-103 PR #846.
21	Cycle-109 T3.6 (commit C, this sprint) removed the conditional branches at
22	the FL orchestrator + model-adapter main() entrypoints; cheval is now
23	operator-facing unconditional. Mock-mode delegation at model-adapter.sh:519-526
24	remains until T3.7 + T3.8 land mock-mode migration under operator approval.
25	
26	All consumers benefit from:
27	- **Chain-walk**: cheval walks the within-company `fallback_chain` (e.g. gpt-5.5-pro → gpt-5.5 → gpt-5.3-codex → codex-headless) on retryable errors (EmptyContent, RateLimited, ProviderOutage, RetriesExhausted).
28	- **Voice-drop**: when a voice's chain exhausts, flatline-orchestrator DROPS that voice from consensus instead of substituting another company's model. Audit log: `consensus.voice_dropped`.
29	- **MODELINV v1.3 envelope**: per-invocation audit record at `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` with `final_model_id`, `transport`, `config_observed`, `models_failed[]`, `models_requested[]`, `capability_evaluation`, `verdict_quality`.
30	- **Verdict-quality envelope** (cycle-109 Sprint 2): every substrate output carries a `verdict_quality` envelope describing voices succeeded/dropped, chain health, blocker_risk, confidence floor, rationale. `status: clean | APPROVED` is definitionally impossible when verdict quality is degraded (NFR-Rel-1).
31	
32	### Rollback (cycle-109 model)
33	
34	**There is no runtime-flag rollback path post-cycle-109.** The
35	`hounfour.flatline_routing` flag is being removed in T3.8 because the
36	legacy adapter it gated is being deleted in T3.7 under explicit
37	operator-approval marker C109.OP-S3. Once Sprint 3 lands on main, the
38	canonical rollback path is:
39	
40	  **`git revert` of the cycle-109 sprint-3 merge commits.**
41	
42	A full rollback runbook lives at
43	`grimoires/loa/runbooks/cycle-109-rollback.md` — covers per-commit revert,
44	config restoration, baseline comparison against
45	`grimoires/loa/cycles/cycle-109-substrate-hardening/baselines/legacy-final-baseline.json`,
46	and CI re-validation. Operators do NOT need to flip a runtime flag; they
47	revert.
48	
49	cycle-124 Sprint 2 (FR-7) — **structured outputs**: `cheval --json-schema FILE`
50	(object root, ≤ 64 KB) is enforced as Anthropic `output_config.format` on
51	catalog entries with the `structured_json` capability and forwarded as
52	`--json-schema` to `claude-headless` (`structured_output` is the answer); other
53	hops run unenforced. The MODELINV envelope records `schema_enforced` and
54	`output_schema_sha256` whenever a schema was requested; the dissent
55	(`adversarial-review.sh`, `dissent-<type>.wire.json`) and Flatline
56	(review/skeptic/scorer wire schemas) parse an enforced payload strictly and keep
57	the tolerant normalize path — with the KF-004 repair loop, now flag-less — only
58	for unenforced voices. Wire schemas live in `.claude/schemas/wire/`; the
59	provider-safe subset is pinned by `tests/unit/wire-schemas-api-safe.bats`. Ratio
60	one-liner over the log:
61	`jq -r 'select(.payload.schema_enforced != null) | [.payload.final_model_id, .payload.schema_enforced] | @tsv' .run/model-invoke.jsonl | sort | uniq -c`.
62	
63	cycle-126 (FR-1) sizes every request from the catalog entry it resolves to.
64	The input bound is a **policy**, not a literal (`loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py`):
65	I1 `estimate + max_tokens ≤ context_window` (the output budget shrinks to a
66	4,096 floor before anything is refused; the envelope records
67	`max_tokens_shrunk`), then I2 — the calibrated value when
68	`ceiling_calibration.calibrated_at` is set, else the `probed_ceiling`
69	(180,000) by default. `LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING=derived` opts into the
70	catalog-derived bound (`context_window − max_tokens`) for an uncalibrated
71	entry: above the probed bound the call proceeds with `preflight_decision:
72	warn` when the count endpoint confirmed the size or the estimate is
73	`low`-uncertainty, and preempts with the calibration command for a `high`
74	one (CJK/emoji-dense text, tool payloads). A provider's own size verdict (HTTP
75	400 prompt-too-long / 413) is **never walked** to the next voice: after one
76	output-budget shrink it exits `CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`, records
77	`.run/ceiling-observed.json` (the bound for that entry until calibration; `/loa`
78	prints it) and names `tools/ceiling-probe-live.py --model <id> --write-catalog`,
79	which folds a measured ceiling, `calibrated_at` and `account_limits` into the
80	catalog. `LOA_CHEVAL_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS=N` lowers any bound;
81	`LOA_CHEVAL_LEGACY_CEILING=1` restores the pre-cycle literal + preempt (no I1,
82	no count). Output defaults: `min(cap, max_output_tokens)` for every provider
83	(64K/16K Anthropic streaming/legacy, 16K elsewhere; 4,096 only without a
84	declaration); `temperature` is absent from the wire unless set;
85	`params.beta_headers` (allowlisted dated flags) join into one `anthropic-beta`
86	header; the health probe asks `/v1/models` first. Envelope fields:
87	`capability_evaluation.{input_ceiling, estimator, max_tokens_shrunk,
88	ceiling_policy, ceiling_unverified, calibration_needed}`.
89	
90	cycle-124 adds one **backstop** (not a rollback): `LOA_CHEVAL_LEGACY_WIRE=1`
91	makes the Anthropic adapter emit the pre-cycle-124 request body (no adaptive
92	`thinking`, no `cache_control` blocks, 4096 default `max_tokens`) so a wire
93	regression can be neutralised without a deploy while the credentialed
94	`live-floor-check.yml` is still unprobed. It removes what cycle-124 ADDED, no
95	more: temperature omission is catalog-driven and stays, and on Opus 5 /
96	Sonnet 5 / Fable the server runs thinking whether or not the block is sent, so
97	pass `--max-tokens` explicitly on those ids under the switch (the
98	`max_tokens` stop warning still fires). The code path stays; reverting is
99	still `git revert` of the cycle-124 unit commits (see the Sprint 1 rollback
100	proof). Env table: `grimoires/loa/runbooks/cheval-delegate-architecture.md`.
101	
102	cycle-129 (FR-8) — **local posture**: under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and health-probe hops are planned only on providers whose model entry says `dispatch_group: local`, each hosted hop refused by name at plan time; the Claude Code session model is exempt and remains the platform, so a local posture keeps model calls local but the session itself still runs against Anthropic. Fewer voices means a DEGRADED verdict quality where the planned voice count is not met — the posture says so in the config comment and in the run output rather than inventing a voice. One fail-closed classifier (`.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py`) serves the shell scripts: an unresolved hop, an unreadable config or a local entry whose fallback chain reaches a hosted entry counts as hosted; an invalid value refuses the run.
103	
104	cycle-129 (FR-7) — **open-weight and local voices**: a local OpenAI-compatible server is declared as a provider (`type: openai_compat`, `keyless: true`, `allow_insecure_endpoint: "<host>"` where the host is a loopback or RFC1918 IP literal or `localhost`; Example 4 in `.loa.config.yaml.example`). The endpoint rule lives once in `.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py` and is used by the cheval loader (`loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py`), the bash wrapper and `model-health-probe.sh --provider <name>`, which probes a configured provider's `/models` with no credential when keyless; at request time a local hop runs with no proxy, no redirects and the declared path prefix. cheval refuses an `http`, loopback or private endpoint without the opt-in at load, for every provider. On the chat-completions path a `structured_json` entry sends `response_format` json_schema and `schema_enforced` is derived from the body sent (one retry without the schema on a server 400 that names it); `reasoning_content`, `reasoning` deltas and a leading `<think>` block go to `thinking` (`thinking_stripped`); an over-window prompt is refused by name. **Advisory voices**: `flatline_protocol.code_review.advisory_voices` and `security_audit.advisory_voices` run beside the counted voices under `advisory_timeout_seconds`; their findings appear only under `advisory_voices[].findings` with `duplicate_of` links and never touch the verdict, the counts or the cost totals — promotion to a counted role needs `hounfour.advisory_promotion`. The budget gate prices each planned voice from the catalog (`loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias … --json`), whose entries now carry `open_weight`, `price_source` and `price_date`. **Bridgebuilder** reads `hounfour.providers`, `hounfour.locality` and `bridgebuilder.exit_on_degraded` from trusted configuration only (locally the working tree; on a pull request the `BRIDGEBUILDER_TRUSTED_CONFIG` repository variable, else the base branch's config, never the head), prints `completed/planned` voices and exits 3 on a DEGRADED consensus (`0` restores the old exit; `entry.sh`'s dependency preflight exits 4).
105	
106	### Verification (cycle-107 sprint-1 + cycle-109 sprint-2/3 cumulative)
107	
108	- FL 3-model run: 549s, 3 voices' MODELINV envelopes recorded, chains populated, all primaries succeeded
109	- RT review: 1 MODELINV envelope, cheval audit signature confirmed
110	- BB: verified via cycle-104 sprint-3 T3.4 (4/4 trials at 297-539KB clean)
111	- **cycle-109 Sprint 2**: 234 new tests; verdict-quality envelope wired through 7/7 IMP-004 consumers; 5 canonical regression fixtures (#807/#809/#823/#868/KF-002 PRD-review) locked in conformance matrix.
112	- **cycle-109 Sprint 3 progress**: T3.1 matrix scaffold + T3.2-T3.5 Cluster B fixes (#864/#863/#793/#820) + T3.6 feature-flag removal + T3.10 activation regression CI workflow. 810-cell matrix wired into `.github/workflows/activation-regression.yml`.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""hop-locality.py — classify model hops as local or hosted for `hounfour.locality: local_voices` (cycle-129 FR-8,
+SDD D-8.0 / D-8.1, DEC-0146).
+
+    python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog <model-config.yaml> --config <.loa.config.yaml> -- <hop>...
+
+One tab-separated line per hop, in the order given:
+
+    <hop> TAB <provider|unknown> TAB <local|hosted> TAB <reason>
+
+A hop is `local` only when ALL of these hold in the merged view (the System Zone catalog overlaid with the project
+config's `hounfour.providers` / `hounfour.aliases`, the two layers cheval merges):
+  * it resolves (a `provider:id` pin, an alias chain, or a bare id that exactly one provider declares) to a model entry
+    that exists;
+  * that model entry, or its provider block, says `dispatch_group: local` (the canonical key, D-8.0);
+  * every hop on the entry's own `fallback_chain` is local by the same rule — cheval walks that chain inside one call,
+    so a local entry that falls back to a hosted one would leave the declared providers without the planner seeing it.
+Everything else is `hosted`: an unresolved hop, an unreadable config, a headless CLI hop (its dispatch group is the
+provider family's), the native session. Fail closed — a hop is never called local because it could not be read.
+
+This file reads declarations only: it never dispatches, never reads credentials and never imports the cheval package
+(run under `-I`, so neither the cwd nor PYTHONPATH reaches sys.path). The request-time rules for a local hop (IP-literal
+or localhost endpoint, no DNS, redirects refused, proxy env ignored, destination logged) are cheval's.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import sys
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+MAX_DEPTH = 10
+
+
+def _merge(base: Any, overlay: Any) -> Any:
+    if isinstance(base, dict) and isinstance(overlay, dict):
+        out = dict(base)
+        for key, value in overlay.items():
+            out[key] = _merge(base.get(key), value) if key in base else value
+        return out
+    return overlay
+
+
+def load_merged(catalog_path: str, config_path: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    import yaml
+
+    with open(catalog_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        catalog = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
+    if not isinstance(catalog, dict):
+        raise ValueError("catalog is not a mapping")
+    merged: Dict[str, Any] = {k: (catalog.get(k) if isinstance(catalog.get(k), dict) else {})
+                              for k in ("providers", "aliases", "backward_compat_aliases")}
+    if config_path:
+        try:
+            with open(config_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+                project = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            project = {}
+        if not isinstance(project, dict):
+            raise ValueError("project config is not a mapping")
+        hounfour = project.get("hounfour")
+        if isinstance(hounfour, dict):
+            for key in ("providers", "aliases"):
+                if isinstance(hounfour.get(key), dict):
+                    merged[key] = _merge(merged.get(key) or {}, hounfour[key])
+    return merged
+
+
+def _alias_target(name: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
+    for table in ("aliases", "backward_compat_aliases"):
+        target = (merged.get(table) or {}).get(name)
+        if isinstance(target, dict):
+            target = target.get("target") or target.get("model")
+        if isinstance(target, str) and target.strip():
+            return target.strip()
+    return None
+
+
+def resolve(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str]]:
+    name = (hop or "").strip()
+    if not name:
+        return None
+    current, seen = name, set()
+    for _ in range(MAX_DEPTH):
+        if ":" in current:
+            provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
+            return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
+        target = _alias_target(current, merged)
+        if not target:
+            break
+        if target in seen:
+            return None
+        seen.add(current)
+        current = target
+    if ":" in current:
+        provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
+        return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
+    providers = merged.get("providers") or {}
+    matches = [p for p, block in providers.items()
+               if isinstance(block, dict) and isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) and current in block["models"]]
+    return (matches[0], current) if len(matches) == 1 else None
+
+
+def classify(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any], _depth: int = 0, _seen: Optional[set] = None) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
+    """(provider, locality, reason) for one hop."""
+    seen = set(_seen or ())
+    target = resolve(hop, merged)
+    if target is None:
+        return "unknown", "hosted", "unresolved"
+    provider, model = target
+    block = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(provider)
+    if not isinstance(block, dict):
+        return provider, "hosted", "provider_not_declared"
+    entry = (block.get("models") or {}).get(model) if isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) else None
+    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
+        return provider, "hosted", "model_not_declared"
+    group = entry.get("dispatch_group") or block.get("dispatch_group") or ""
+    if group != "local":
+        return provider, "hosted", f"dispatch_group={group or 'unset'}"
+    key = f"{provider}:{model}"
+    if key in seen:
+        return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"
+    seen.add(key)
+    chain = entry.get("fallback_chain") or []
+    if not isinstance(chain, list):
+        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
+    if _depth >= MAX_DEPTH:
+        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_too_deep"
+    for nxt in chain:
+        if not isinstance(nxt, str):
+            return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
+        p2, loc, _ = classify(nxt, merged, _depth + 1, seen)
+        if loc != "local":
+            return provider, "hosted", f"fallback_chain_reaches_hosted:{nxt}({p2})"
+    return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"
+
+
+def _clean(text: str) -> str:
+    return "".join(c if c.isprintable() and c not in "\t" else "_" for c in text)[:128]
+
+
+def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
+    ap.add_argument("--catalog", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--config", default="")
+    ap.add_argument("hops", nargs="*")
+    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        merged = load_merged(args.catalog, args.config or None)
+        err = ""
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail closed: every hop hosted, the reason said once
+        merged, err = None, f"{type(exc).__name__}"
+        print(f"hop-locality: the merged config could not be read ({err}) — every hop is hosted", file=sys.stderr)
+    for hop in args.hops:
+        if merged is None:
+            print(f"{_clean(hop)}\tunknown\thosted\tconfig_unreadable")
+            continue
+        provider, loc, reason = classify(hop, merged)
+        print(f"{_clean(hop)}\t{_clean(provider)}\t{loc}\t{_clean(reason)}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""hop-locality.py — classify model hops as local or hosted for `hounfour.locality: local_voices` (cycle-129 FR-8,
+SDD D-8.0 / D-8.1, DEC-0146).
+
+    python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog <model-config.yaml> --config <.loa.config.yaml> -- <hop>...
+
+One tab-separated line per hop, in the order given:
+
+    <hop> TAB <provider|unknown> TAB <local|hosted> TAB <reason>
+
+A hop is `local` only when ALL of these hold in the merged view (the System Zone catalog overlaid with the project
+config's `hounfour.providers` / `hounfour.aliases`, the two layers cheval merges):
+  * it resolves (a `provider:id` pin, an alias chain, or a bare id that exactly one provider declares) to a model entry
+    that exists;
+  * that model entry, or its provider block, says `dispatch_group: local` (the canonical key, D-8.0);
+  * every hop on the entry's own `fallback_chain` is local by the same rule — cheval walks that chain inside one call,
+    so a local entry that falls back to a hosted one would leave the declared providers without the planner seeing it.
+Everything else is `hosted`: an unresolved hop, an unreadable config, a headless CLI hop (its dispatch group is the
+provider family's), the native session. Fail closed — a hop is never called local because it could not be read.
+
+This file reads declarations only: it never dispatches, never reads credentials and never imports the cheval package
+(run under `-I`, so neither the cwd nor PYTHONPATH reaches sys.path). The request-time rules for a local hop (IP-literal
+or localhost endpoint, no DNS, redirects refused, proxy env ignored, destination logged) are cheval's.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import sys
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+MAX_DEPTH = 10
+
+
+def _merge(base: Any, overlay: Any) -> Any:
+    if isinstance(base, dict) and isinstance(overlay, dict):
+        out = dict(base)
+        for key, value in overlay.items():
+            out[key] = _merge(base.get(key), value) if key in base else value
+        return out
+    return overlay
+
+
+def load_merged(catalog_path: str, config_path: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    import yaml
+
+    with open(catalog_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        catalog = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
+    if not isinstance(catalog, dict):
+        raise ValueError("catalog is not a mapping")
+    merged: Dict[str, Any] = {k: (catalog.get(k) if isinstance(catalog.get(k), dict) else {})
+                              for k in ("providers", "aliases", "backward_compat_aliases")}
+    if config_path:
+        try:
+            with open(config_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+                project = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            project = {}
+        if not isinstance(project, dict):
+            raise ValueError("project config is not a mapping")
+        hounfour = project.get("hounfour")
+        if isinstance(hounfour, dict):
+            for key in ("providers", "aliases"):
+                if isinstance(hounfour.get(key), dict):
+                    merged[key] = _merge(merged.get(key) or {}, hounfour[key])
+    return merged
+
+
+def _alias_target(name: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
+    for table in ("aliases", "backward_compat_aliases"):
+        target = (merged.get(table) or {}).get(name)
+        if isinstance(target, dict):
+            target = target.get("target") or target.get("model")
+        if isinstance(target, str) and target.strip():
+            return target.strip()
+    return None
+
+
+def resolve(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str]]:
+    name = (hop or "").strip()
+    if not name:
+        return None
+    current, seen = name, set()
+    for _ in range(MAX_DEPTH):
+        if ":" in current:
+            provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
+            return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
+        target = _alias_target(current, merged)
+        if not target:
+            break
+        if target in seen:
+            return None
+        seen.add(current)
+        current = target
+    if ":" in current:
+        provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
+        return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
+    providers = merged.get("providers") or {}
+    matches = [p for p, block in providers.items()
+               if isinstance(block, dict) and isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) and current in block["models"]]
+    return (matches[0], current) if len(matches) == 1 else None
+
+
+def classify(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any], _depth: int = 0, _seen: Optional[set] = None) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
+    """(provider, locality, reason) for one hop."""
+    seen = set(_seen or ())
+    target = resolve(hop, merged)
+    if target is None:
+        return "unknown", "hosted", "unresolved"
+    provider, model = target
+    block = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(provider)
+    if not isinstance(block, dict):
+        return provider, "hosted", "provider_not_declared"
+    entry = (block.get("models") or {}).get(model) if isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) else None
+    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
+        return provider, "hosted", "model_not_declared"
+    group = entry.get("dispatch_group") or block.get("dispatch_group") or ""
+    if group != "local":
+        return provider, "hosted", f"dispatch_group={group or 'unset'}"
+    key = f"{provider}:{model}"
+    if key in seen:
+        return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"
+    seen.add(key)
+    chain = entry.get("fallback_chain") or []
+    if not isinstance(chain, list):
+        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
+    if _depth >= MAX_DEPTH:
+        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_too_deep"
+    for nxt in chain:
+        if not isinstance(nxt, str):
+            return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
+        p2, loc, _ = classify(nxt, merged, _depth + 1, seen)
+        if loc != "local":
+            return provider, "hosted", f"fallback_chain_reaches_hosted:{nxt}({p2})"
+    return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"
+
+
+def _clean(text: str) -> str:
+    return "".join(c if c.isprintable() and c not in "\t" else "_" for c in text)[:128]
+
+
+def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
+    ap.add_argument("--catalog", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--config", default="")
+    ap.add_argument("hops", nargs="*")
+    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        merged = load_merged(args.catalog, args.config or None)
+        err = ""
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail closed: every hop hosted, the reason said once
+        merged, err = None, f"{type(exc).__name__}"
+        print(f"hop-locality: the merged config could not be read ({err}) — every hop is hosted", file=sys.stderr)
+    for hop in args.hops:
+        if merged is None:
+            print(f"{_clean(hop)}\tunknown\thosted\tconfig_unreadable")
+            continue
+        provider, loc, reason = classify(hop, merged)
+        print(f"{_clean(hop)}\t{_clean(provider)}\t{loc}\t{_clean(reason)}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+    return 0
+}

Based on my examination of the PR, I have found several candidate defects. Let me compile my findings:

## Evidence Findings

**head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1494 — Unquoted variable expansion in jq output assignment — PROBE_HTTP set to empty string instead of number — critical severity — high confidence**

Line 1494: `PROBE_HTTP=""` when auth_env is missing. Later at line 1512, `PROBE_HTTP="$HTTP_STATUS"` expects numeric status. The test at line 1594 (`[[ "$PROBE_ERROR_CLASS" != "auth" ]] || [[ -n "$PROBE_HTTP" && "$PROBE_HTTP" != "0" ]]`) will fail to properly detect auth-class no-call probes when PROBE_HTTP is empty string vs "0". The logic branches on whether an HTTP call occurred; empty string passes the `-n` test (is non-empty), making `[[ -n "" ]]` false when the intent is to skip cost increment only when no call was made.

Line 1494: `PROBE_HTTP=""` when auth_env is unset. This will fail the probe budget test at 1594 which checks `[[ -n "$PROBE_HTTP" && "$PROBE_HTTP" != "0" ]]`. When PROBE_HTTP="", the condition becomes `[[ -n "" && "" != "0" ]]` = false, so the cost IS incremented even though no HTTP call was made — burning budget on missing credentials.

**head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1501 — Same PROBE_HTTP empty-string bug at second auth failure point — critical severity — high confidence**

Line 1501: `PROBE_HTTP=""` when provider auth is neither {env:VAR} nor keyless. Same symptom as line 1494: the global is empty string, the budget gate at 1594 will increment cost for a no-call case.

**head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1477 — jq -r output from endpoint validator stderr will contain shell-unsafe characters — high severity — medium confidence**

Line 1477: `PROBE_REASON="endpoint refused: $(jq -r '"[" + (.code // "?") + "] " + (.detail // "")' "$verr" 2>/dev/null | head -c 300)"`. The jq expression will fail silently (2>/dev/null) if $verr does not contain valid JSON, leaving PROBE_REASON truncated. If endpoint_validator outputs non-JSON on error, the jq parse fails and the reason becomes incomplete (just "endpoint refused: "). The 2>/dev/null silently eats both the error and the incomplete output.

**head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1576 — _configured_providers subprocess will lose exit code under set -e — high severity — high confidence**

Line 1576: `if [[ "$provider" =~ $_CONFIGURED_NAME_RE ]] && _configured_providers | grep -qxF -- "$provider"; then`. The pipeline `_configured_providers | grep -qxF` will exit with grep's code (0 if match found, 1 if not), BUT inside the subshell at line 877-891, `_configured_providers` has `return 0` at line 890 unconditionally. If `_endpoint_policy_cli` fails (exits non-zero), the function still returns 0 at line 890, so the pipe never fails. This means a failed configured provider lookup will be silently treated as "provider not found" (no match) rather than propagating the config-load error.

**head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:898-909 — Inconsistent return semantics between _registry_models paths — high severity — high confidence**

The builtin-provider path (lines 919-928) uses `yq eval ... 2>/dev/null | sed ...` and returns 0 implicitly. The configured-provider path (lines 904-908) returns 1 on `_configured_provider_json` failure. At line 1576 and during --dry-run, the caller will see different exit codes for the same logical "no models found" case: configured path returns 1, builtin path returns 0. The `_probe_all` loop at line 1672 feeds `_registry_models` output into a while loop; a failed `_registry_models` should exit non-zero to signal an error, but the builtin path never does.

**head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:904 — Unquoted printf with model_id — critical severity — high confidence**

Line 906: `printf '%s %s\n' "$provider" "$m"`. If `$m` contains %, this will be interpreted as a format string by printf. Although the format string is literal '%s %s\n', a malicious model entry from the config could inject format-string exploits into the output.

**head/tests/unit/model-health-probe-configured-provider.bats:78-83 — HTTP endpoint without opt-in assertion is wrong — high severity — high confidence**

Line 82: `[[ "$output" == *"ENDPOINT-INSECURE-SCHEME"* ]]`. The probe's _configured_provider_json calls endpoint_validator__check at line 1475, which should reject HTTP without opt-in. But the error message comes from the endpoint_validator, NOT the probe script. #!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.3 (PRD FR-7 AC-7.5, SDD D-7.4, D-7.6).
#
# The dissent budget pre-check prices every planned voice — the primary, the companion's first hop, each advisory voice —
# at its catalog price (python3 -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias), instead of the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok.
# An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 for that voice and is said by name; a zero-priced entry estimates
# zero and is said too. Prices come from fixture entries in the test's project config (hounfour.providers overlays the
# catalog, as cheval merges it). Each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 × output rate, micro-USD/Mtok → cents.
# =============================================================================

load adversarial-review-s3-helpers

setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3bud; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
teardown() { s3_teardown; }

_cfg() {  # <model> <budget> <companion_voice> [extra code_review lines]
    s3_config "hounfour:
  providers:
    openai:
      models:
        fixture-priced:
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 2000000, output_per_mtok: 8000000}
    fixturelocal:
      models:
        fixture-zero:
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0}
        fixture-stale:
          price_date: \"2000-01-01\"
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 1000000, output_per_mtok: 1000000}
flatline_protocol:
  code_review:
    enabled: true
    model: $1
    budget_cents: $2
    timeout_seconds: 30
    companion_voice: $3
    fallback_chain: []
${4:-}"
}

_big_diff() {  # a diff whose estimate is 1,000,500 input tokens (3,000,000 bytes / 3 + 500)
    { printf 'diff --git a/x.sh b/x.sh\n'; head -c $(( 3000000 - 25 )) /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a'; } > "$T/diff.patch"
    [ "$(wc -c < "$T/diff.patch")" -eq 3000000 ]
}

@test "BUD-1 the primary is priced at its catalog rate (no fixed-rate fallback): 1,000,500 tokens × 2 + 2000 × 8 USD/Mtok = 201c" {
    _big_diff
    _cfg fixture-priced 150 false
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.status' <<<"$result")" = "budget_exceeded" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "201" ]
    [ "$(jq -c '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | {role, alias, estimated_cents, pricing_source}]' <<<"$result")" = '[{"role":"primary","alias":"fixture-priced","estimated_cents":201,"pricing_source":"config"}]' ]
    grep -qF "budget: estimate 201c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-priced 201c)" "$T/stderr.log"
    ! grep -q "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "a catalog-priced primary fell back"; return 1; }
    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
}

@test "BUD-2 an alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok for that voice, said by name (1000c + 6c)" {
    _big_diff
    _cfg mystery-model-x 150 false
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.estimate_voices[0].pricing_source' <<<"$result")" = "fallback" ]
    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (primary) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice" "$T/stderr.log"
    [ "$(grep -c "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log")" = "1" ]
}

@test "BUD-3 a zero-priced entry estimates 0c and is said: a 0-cent budget admits it, where the fixed rate would refuse" {
    _cfg fixture-zero 0 false
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (primary) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qF "budget: estimate 0c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-zero 0c)" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qx "fixture-zero" "$CALLS"
    # the same run priced at the fixed rate is refused (the regression this replaces: 2000 output tokens × 30 = 6c > 0)
    _cfg mystery-model-x 0 false
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
}

@test "BUD-4 the gate sums every planned voice: primary + the companion's first hop + each advisory voice" {
    _big_diff
    _cfg fixture-priced 1 true "    advisory_voices: [fixture-zero, mystery-model-x]"
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    [ "$(jq -r '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | "\(.role)=\(.alias)"] | join(" ")' <<<"$result")" = "primary=fixture-priced companion=claude-headless advisory=fixture-zero advisory=mystery-model-x" ]
    # the companion's price is the catalog's (whatever it is today): recompute it from the same CLI
    local row ci co comp
    row=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias claude-headless --config "$CONFIG_FILE")
    ci=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$row"); co=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$row")
    [[ "$ci" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$co" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
    comp=$(( 1000500 * ci / 10000000000 + 2000 * co / 10000000000 ))
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[1].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "$comp" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[2].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "0" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[3].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "$(( 201 + comp + 0 + 1006 ))" ]
    [ "$(jq '[.metadata.estimate_voices[].estimated_cents] | add' <<<"$result")" = "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" ]
    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (advisory) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (advisory)" "$T/stderr.log"
}

@test "BUD-5 a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) is used as given and said" {
    _cfg fixture-stale 1000 false
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    grep -qF "budget: fixture-stale (primary) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given" "$T/stderr.log"
}

@test "BUD-6 with no price CLI answer at all every voice falls back and is said (the gate never prices from nothing)" {
    _cfg fixture-priced 1000 false
    # a PYTHONPATH that cannot import the package: the CLI fails, every planned voice is unknown
    local real patched
    real="$(declare -f _adv_budget_estimate)"
    patched="${real/PYTHONPATH=\"\$PROJECT_ROOT\/.claude\/adapters\"/PYTHONPATH=/nonexistent}"
    [ "$patched" != "$real" ]   # (the seam was found: the CLI really cannot be imported in this run)
    eval "$patched"
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ]
    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for fixture-priced (primary)" "$T/stderr.log"
}

However, on line 682, it checks `Object.entries(head)`, which would iterate an empty array. This is technically correct (no refusals if head unparsable), but **a subtle assumption**: line 678 assumes that if head is unparsable, it "declares nothing Bridgebuilder would admit". The code is correct but could be clearer — consider: what if head YAML is unparsable due to a file-read error vs. syntax error? The comment says "an unparsable head declares nothing", but this silently drops any declarations it might have had. No security issue (fail-closed), but the logic is non-obvious.

This is correct per the SDD (refuse by name after planning), but the test comment says "a refused planned voice never clears a merge" (line 405), which is asserted on the result, not the planning list. The logic is correct but **the assertion sequence could mislead readers**: line 404 tests `voicesPlanned` (which includes refused voices), line 405 tests the merge verdict. This is the intended behavior (refused voices ARE planned but never dispatched), but the test name and assertion order could be clearer.

Looking at multi-model-pipeline.ts:650-675, `computeVerdictBand()` only uses the `status` and `chain_health` fields of `verdictQuality`, so this is fine. **No defect**, but the stripped context means error messages in computeVerdictBand cannot name the model.

This is correct, but **a subtle assumption**: the code assumes `verdicts` is always an array. This is correct per the design, but **the test on line 245 verifies this** — good. +++ b/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py
@@ -0,0 +1,238 @@
+"""Per-provider endpoint policy on the cheval Python path (cycle-129 FR-7, SDD D-7.2, D-8.0).
+
+The rule, applied at config load to every HTTP provider in the merged ``hounfour.providers`` view:
+
+* ``allow_insecure_endpoint`` is a host STRING, never a boolean. It must be an IP literal or ``localhost``
+  (an insecure endpoint is never resolved through DNS, so there is no rebinding), and the address must be
+  loopback (``127.0.0.0/8``, ``::1``) or RFC1918 (``10/8``, ``172.16/12``, ``192.168/16``). Link-local,
+  the cloud metadata addresses, unique-local IPv6 and every public range are refused.
+* An ``http://`` endpoint is admitted only when its host equals the provider's opt-in host. A mismatched
+  host, a public ``http`` host or an ``http`` endpoint without an opt-in fails at load with a named reason.
+* Every other endpoint keeps the cycle-099 refusals: ``https`` only, no userinfo, no control bytes or path
+  traversal, and no loopback, private, link-local, metadata or otherwise blocked IP literal (``localhost``
+  included). One provider's opt-in never changes another provider's checks.
+* ``keyless: true`` marks a provider that needs no credential; a literal ``auth: "local"`` is accepted and
+  normalised to ``keyless: true`` in the merged view. A keyless provider is admitted only when every model
+  declares ``context_window`` and ``dispatch_group``.
+
+ONE implementation: every URL and opt-in decision here is made by the canonical
+``.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py`` (the module the bash callers and the health probe use),
+loaded by path as ``loa_cheval.codegen.emit_endpoint_validator_ts`` does: ``check_insecure_optin`` for the
+opt-in and ``validate_declared_endpoint`` (the full pipeline minus the host allowlist, which an
+operator-declared https host is not on) for the endpoint. The refusal codes are therefore the validator's
+codes, and URL parsing stays confined to that module (the cycle-099 import guard).
+``tests/test_endpoint_validator_optin.py`` runs one case table through both entry points.
+
+Request-time half (``TransportPolicy`` in ``providers/base.py``): for an opted-in provider, or a model whose
+``dispatch_group`` is ``local``, the adapter ignores proxy environment variables, refuses HTTP redirects and
+requires every request URL to stay under the declared endpoint path.
+
+CLI (used by ``model-health-probe.sh --provider <name>``; reads the merged config, never prints a secret)::
+
+    python3 -m loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy list-providers [--project-root DIR]
+    python3 -m loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy describe-provider NAME [--project-root DIR]
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+import threading
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+from loa_cheval.types import ConfigError
+
+# The literal auth values normalised to keyless (D-8.0). Only "local": any other literal could be a real key.
+KEYLESS_AUTH_LITERALS = frozenset({"local"})
+
+# .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py → .claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py
+_VALIDATOR_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "scripts" / "lib" / "endpoint-validator.py"
+_VALIDATOR: Any = None
+_VALIDATOR_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+
+
+def _validator() -> Any:
+    """The canonical endpoint-validator module, loaded once by path. A missing
+    or unloadable validator is a ConfigError (fail-closed: no endpoint is
+    admitted unchecked)."""
+    global _VALIDATOR
+    with _VALIDATOR_LOCK:
+        if _VALIDATOR is not None:
+            return _VALIDATOR
+        name = "loa_endpoint_validator_canonical"
+        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, _VALIDATOR_PATH)
+        if spec is None or spec.loader is None or not _VALIDATOR_PATH.is_file():
+            raise ConfigError(f"[ENDPOINT-VALIDATOR-MISSING] {_VALIDATOR_PATH} not found; reinstall the framework")
+        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+        sys.modules[name] = module
+        try:
+            spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — any load failure is fail-closed
+            sys.modules.pop(name, None)
+            raise ConfigError(f"[ENDPOINT-VALIDATOR-MISSING] {_VALIDATOR_PATH} failed to load: {exc}") from exc
+        _VALIDATOR = module
+        return module
+
+
+class EndpointPolicyError(ConfigError):
+    """A provider endpoint or opt-in refused at load. ``policy_code`` is the endpoint-validator code."""
+
+    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str, provider: Optional[str] = None):
+        where = f"providers.{provider}: " if provider else ""
+        super().__init__(f"[{code}] {where}{detail}", context={"policy_code": code, "provider": provider})
+        self.policy_code = code
+        self.detail = detail
+
+
+def split_url(url: str) -> Tuple[str, str, Optional[int], str]:
+    """(scheme, canonical host, explicit port or None, path) via the canonical validator; ValueError on a bad URL."""
+    return _validator().split_url(url)
+
+
+def canonical_optin_host(value: Any, provider: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
+    """Validate an ``allow_insecure_endpoint`` value and return its canonical host, or raise."""
+    ok, code, detail, host = _validator().check_insecure_optin(value)
+    if not ok:
+        raise EndpointPolicyError(code or "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-INVALID", detail or "invalid opt-in", provider)
+    return host
+
+
+def check_endpoint(endpoint: str, allow_insecure_endpoint: Any = None, provider: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Apply the D-7.2 rule to one provider's endpoint. Returns the canonical opt-in host (or None); raises."""
+    optin = canonical_optin_host(allow_insecure_endpoint, provider) if allow_insecure_endpoint is not None else None
+    result = _validator().validate_declared_endpoint(endpoint, allow_insecure_endpoint=optin)
+    if not result.valid:
+        raise EndpointPolicyError(result.code or "ENDPOINT-INVALID", result.detail or "endpoint refused", provider)
+    return optin
+
+
+# --- the merged view --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _is_cli_provider(prov: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    ptype = str(prov.get("type") or "")
+    if ptype.endswith("-headless"):
+        return True
+    models = prov.get("models") or {}
+    return bool(models) and isinstance(models, dict) and all(
+        isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("kind") == "cli" for m in models.values()
+    )
+
+
+def normalise_keyless(merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Pre-interpolation step: a literal ``auth: "local"`` becomes ``keyless: true`` (D-8.0); ``keyless`` must be a bool."""
+    providers = merged.get("providers")
+    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
+        return
+    for name, prov in providers.items():
+        if not isinstance(prov, dict):
+            continue
+        if "keyless" in prov and not isinstance(prov["keyless"], bool):
+            raise ConfigError(
+                f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.keyless must be true or false, got {prov['keyless']!r}"
+            )
+        auth = prov.get("auth")
+        if isinstance(auth, str) and auth.strip().lower() in KEYLESS_AUTH_LITERALS:
+            prov["keyless"] = True
+
+
+def validate_providers(merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Post-interpolation step: endpoint rule and keyless preconditions for every provider."""
+    providers = merged.get("providers")
+    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
+        return
+    for name, prov in providers.items():
+        if not isinstance(prov, dict):
+            continue
+        optin = prov.get("allow_insecure_endpoint")
+        endpoint = prov.get("endpoint")
+        if not _is_cli_provider(prov) and endpoint not in (None, ""):
+            if not isinstance(endpoint, str):
+                raise ConfigError(f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.endpoint must be a string")
+            check_endpoint(endpoint, optin, name)
+        elif optin is not None:
+            # An opt-in with nothing to apply to is still validated, so a typo never sits silent.
+            canonical_optin_host(optin, name)
+        if prov.get("keyless") is True:
+            models = prov.get("models") or {}
+            if not isinstance(models, dict) or not models:
+                raise ConfigError(f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name} is keyless but declares no models")
+            for model_id, model in models.items():
+                model = model if isinstance(model, dict) else {}
+                cw = model.get("context_window")
+                if not isinstance(cw, int) or isinstance(cw, bool) or cw <= 0:
+                    raise ConfigError(
+                        f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.models.{model_id}: a keyless provider is admitted only "
+                        f"with a declared context_window (a positive integer)"
+                    )
+                if not model.get("dispatch_group"):
+                    raise ConfigError(
+                        f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.models.{model_id}: a keyless provider is admitted only "
+                        f"with a declared dispatch_group"
+                    )
+
+
+# --- probe helper CLI -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_ENV_AUTH = re.compile(r"^\{env:([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}$")
+
+
+def describe_provider(merged: Dict[str, Any], name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """What the health probe needs about one configured provider. Never carries a secret value."""
+    prov = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(name)
+    if not isinstance(prov, dict):
+        raise KeyError(name)
+    raw_auth = getattr(prov.get("auth"), "_raw", prov.get("auth"))
+    auth_env = None
+    if isinstance(raw_auth, str):
+        m = _ENV_AUTH.match(raw_auth.strip())
+        if m:
+            auth_env = m.group(1)
+    optin = prov.get("allow_insecure_endpoint")
+    models = prov.get("models") or {}
+    return {
+        "name": name,

index 0d9b3622..fbd50572 100644
--- a/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/pricing.py
+++ b/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/pricing.py
@@ -6,6 +6,7 @@ No floating-point anywhere in the cost path.
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import datetime as _dt
 import logging
 import re
 
@@ -64,6 +65,13 @@ class PricingEntry:
     long_context_threshold: Optional[int] = None
     long_context_input_multiplier: float = 1.0
     long_context_output_multiplier: float = 1.0
+    # cycle-129 FR-7 (SDD D-7.6): catalog provenance, read from the model entry
+    # (siblings of `pricing`). `price_date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`; a date older than
+    # STALE_PRICE_DAYS marks the price stale (ledger `pricing_source:
+    # stale_catalog`). Absent on every entry today — no behaviour change.
+    open_weight: bool = False
+    price_source: Optional[str] = None
+    price_date: Optional[str] = None
 
 
 @dataclass
@@ -303,9 +311,68 @@ def _exact_pricing(
         cache_read_per_mtok=_int_rate(pricing.get("cache_read_per_mtok"), input_per_mtok // 10),
         cache_write_per_mtok=_int_rate(pricing.get("cache_write_per_mtok"), input_per_mtok * 5 // 4),
         **_long_context_fields(pricing.get("long_context")),
+        **_provenance_fields(model_config),
     )
 
 
+def _provenance_fields(model_config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """cycle-129 D-7.6: `open_weight`, `price_source`, `price_date` from the model entry (strings kept as given;
+    a non-string is dropped — the catalog test is where a malformed value fails, never the cost path)."""
+    out: Dict[str, Any] = {"open_weight": model_config.get("open_weight") is True}
+    for key in ("price_source", "price_date"):
+        value = model_config.get(key)
+        if isinstance(value, _dt.date):   # YAML reads an unquoted 2026-10-14 as a date
+            value = value.isoformat()
+        if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():
+            out[key] = value.strip()
+    return out
+
+
+# cycle-129 D-7.6: a catalog price older than this is stale.
+STALE_PRICE_DAYS = 90
+_PRICE_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")
+_STALE_WARNED: set = set()
+
+
+def price_date_of(entry: Optional[PricingEntry]) -> Optional[_dt.date]:
+    """The entry's `price_date` as a date, or None when absent or not a valid `YYYY-MM-DD`."""
+    raw = getattr(entry, "price_date", None)
+    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not _PRICE_DATE_RE.match(raw):
+        return None
+    try:
+        return _dt.date.fromisoformat(raw)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def price_is_stale(entry: Optional[PricingEntry], today: Optional[_dt.date] = None) -> bool:
+    """True when the entry carries a `price_date` older than STALE_PRICE_DAYS (an entry without one is not stale:
+    provenance is required only of open-weight non-zero prices, and the catalog test enforces that)."""
+    date = price_date_of(entry)
+    if date is None:
+        return False
+    today = today or _dt.datetime.now(_dt.timezone.utc).date()
+    return (today - date).days > STALE_PRICE_DAYS
+
+
+def pricing_source_for(entry: Optional[PricingEntry], today: Optional[_dt.date] = None) -> str:
+    """`config` for a catalog price, `stale_catalog` for one whose `price_date` is past STALE_PRICE_DAYS (WARNed once
+    per entry per process), `unknown` for no price."""
+    if entry is None:
+        return "unknown"
+    if price_is_stale(entry, today):
+        key = (entry.provider, entry.model)
+        if key not in _STALE_WARNED:
+            _STALE_WARNED.add(key)
+            logger.warning(
+                "pricing: the catalog price of %s:%s is dated %s, older than %d days — recorded as stale_catalog; "
+                "re-check it against its price_source (%s)",
+                entry.provider, entry.model, entry.price_date, STALE_PRICE_DAYS, entry.price_source or "none given",
+            )
+        return "stale_catalog"
+    return "config"

+"""Per-provider endpoint policy on the cheval Python path (cycle-129 FR-7, SDD D-7.2, D-8.0).
+
+The rule, applied at config load to every HTTP provider in the merged ``hounfour.providers`` view:
+
+* ``allow_insecure_endpoint`` is a host STRING, never a boolean. It must be an IP literal or ``localhost``
+  (an insecure endpoint is never resolved through DNS, so there is no rebinding), and the address must be
+  loopback (``127.0.0.0/8``, ``::1``) or RFC1918 (``10/8``, ``172.16/12``, ``192.168/16``). Link-local,
+  the cloud metadata addresses, unique-local IPv6 and every public range are refused.
+* An ``http://`` endpoint is admitted only when its host equals the provider's opt-in host. A mismatched
+  host, a public ``http`` host or an ``http`` endpoint without an opt-in fails at load with a named reason.
+* Every other endpoint keeps the cycle-099 refusals: ``https`` only, no userinfo, no control bytes or path
+  traversal, and no loopback, private, link-local, metadata or otherwise blocked IP literal (``localhost``
+  included). One provider's opt-in never changes another provider's checks.
+* ``keyless: true`` marks a provider that needs no credential; a literal ``auth: "local"`` is accepted and
+  normalised to ``keyless: true`` in the merged view. A keyless provider is admitted only when every model
+  declares ``context_window`` and ``dispatch_group``.
+
+ONE implementation: every URL and opt-in decision here is made by the canonical
+``.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py`` (the module the bash callers and the health probe use),
+loaded by path as ``loa_cheval.codegen.emit_endpoint_validator_ts`` does: ``check_insecure_optin`` for the
+opt-in and ``validate_declared_endpoint`` (the full pipeline minus the host allowlist, which an
+operator-declared https host is not on) for the endpoint. The refusal codes are therefore the validator's
+codes, and URL parsing stays confined to that module (the cycle-099 import guard).
+``tests/test_endpoint_validator_optin.py`` runs one case table through both entry points.
+
+Request-time half (``TransportPolicy`` in ``providers/base.py``): for an opted-in provider, or a model whose
+``dispatch_group`` is ``local``, the adapter ignores proxy environment variables, refuses HTTP redirects and
+requires every request URL to stay under the declared endpoint path.
+
+CLI (used by ``model-health-probe.sh --provider <name>``; reads the merged config, never prints a secret)::
+
+    python3 -m loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy list-providers [--project-root DIR]
+    python3 -m loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy describe-provider NAME [--project-root DIR]
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+import threading
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+from loa_cheval.types import ConfigError
+
+# The literal auth values normalised to keyless (D-8.0). Only "local": any other literal could be a real key.
+KEYLESS_AUTH_LITERALS = frozenset({"local"})
+
+# .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py → .claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py
+_VALIDATOR_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "scripts" / "lib" / "endpoint-validator.py"
+_VALIDATOR: Any = None
+_VALIDATOR_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+
+
+def _validator() -> Any:
+    """The canonical endpoint-validator module, loaded once by path. A missing
+    or unloadable validator is a ConfigError (fail-closed: no endpoint is
+    admitted unchecked)."""
+    global _VALIDATOR
+    with _VALIDATOR_LOCK:
+        if _VALIDATOR is not None:
+            return _VALIDATOR
+        name = "loa_endpoint_validator_canonical"
+        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, _VALIDATOR_PATH)
+        if spec is None or spec.loader is None or not _VALIDATOR_PATH.is_file():
+            raise ConfigError(f"[ENDPOINT-VALIDATOR-MISSING] {_VALIDATOR_PATH} not found; reinstall the framework")
+        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+        sys.modules[name] = module
+        try:
+            spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — any load failure is fail-closed
+            sys.modules.pop(name, None)
+            raise ConfigError(f"[ENDPOINT-VALIDATOR-MISSING] {_VALIDATOR_PATH} failed to load: {exc}") from exc
+        _VALIDATOR = module
+        return module
+
+
+class EndpointPolicyError(ConfigError):
+    """A provider endpoint or opt-in refused at load. ``policy_code`` is the endpoint-validator code."""
+
+    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str, provider: Optional[str] = None):
+        where = f"providers.{provider}: " if provider else ""
+        super().__init__(f"[{code}] {where}{detail}", context={"policy_code": code, "provider": provider})
+        self.policy_code = code
+        self.detail = detail
+
+
+def split_url(url: str) -> Tuple[str, str, Optional[int], str]:
+    """(scheme, canonical host, explicit port or None, path) via the canonical validator; ValueError on a bad URL."""
+    return _validator().split_url(url)

+

+    return host

+
+def check_endpoint(endpoint: str, allow_insecure_endpoint: Any = None, provider: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Apply the D-7.2 rule to one provider's endpoint. Returns the canonical opt-in host (or None); raises."""
+    optin = canonical_optin_host(allow_insecure_endpoint, provider) if allow_insecure_endpoint is not None else None

+    if not result.valid:

+    return optin

+
+# --- the merged view --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+

+def _is_cli_provider(prov: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    ptype = str(prov.get("type") or "")
+    if ptype.endswith("-headless"):
+        return True
+    models = prov.get("models") or {}
+    return bool(models) and isinstance(models, dict) and all(
+        isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("kind") == "cli" for m in models.values()

+
+
+def normalise_keyless(merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Pre-interpolation step: a literal ``auth: "local"`` becomes ``keyless: true`` (D-8.0); ``keyless`` must be a bool."""
+    providers = merged.get("providers")
+    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
+        return
+    for name, prov in providers.items():
+        if not isinstance(prov, dict):
+            continue
+        if "keyless" in prov and not isinstance(prov["keyless"], bool):
+            raise ConfigError(
+                f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.keyless must be true or false, got {prov['keyless']!r}"
+            )
+        auth = prov.get("auth")
+        if isinstance(auth, str) and auth.strip().lower() in KEYLESS_AUTH_LITERALS:
+            prov["keyless"] = True
+
+
+def validate_providers(merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Post-interpolation step: endpoint rule and keyless preconditions for every provider."""
+    providers = merged.get("providers")
+    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
+        return
+    for name, prov in providers.items():
+        if not isinstance(prov, dict):
+            continue
+        optin = prov.get("allow_insecure_endpoint")
+        endpoint = prov.get("endpoint")
+        if not _is_cli_provider(prov) and endpoint not in (None, ""):
+            if not isinstance(endpoint, str):
+                raise ConfigError(f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.endpoint must be a string")
+            check_endpoint(endpoint, optin, name)
+        elif optin is not None:
+            # An opt-in with nothing to apply to is still validated, so a typo never sits silent.
+            canonical_optin_host(optin, name)
+        if prov.get("keyless") is True:
+            models = prov.get("models") or {}
+            if not isinstance(models, dict) or not models:
+                raise ConfigError(f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name} is keyless but declares no models")
+            for model_id, model in models.items():
+                model = model if isinstance(model, dict) else {}
+                cw = model.get("context_window")
+                if not isinstance(cw, int) or isinstance(cw, bool) or cw <= 0:
+                    raise ConfigError(
+                        f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.models.{model_id}: a keyless provider is admitted only "
+                        f"with a declared context_window (a positive integer)"

+                if not model.get("dispatch_group"):
+                    raise ConfigError(
+                        f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.models.{model_id}: a keyless provider is admitted only "
+                        f"with a declared dispatch_group"
+                    )
+
+
+# --- probe helper CLI -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_ENV_AUTH = re.compile(r"^\{env:([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}$")
+
+
+def describe_provider(merged: Dict[str, Any], name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """What the health probe needs about one configured provider. Never carries a secret value."""
+    prov = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(name)
+    if not isinstance(prov, dict):
+        raise KeyError(name)
+    raw_auth = getattr(prov.get("auth"), "_raw", prov.get("auth"))
+    auth_env = None
+    if isinstance(raw_auth, str):
+        m = _ENV_AUTH.match(raw_auth.strip())
+        if m:
+            auth_env = m.group(1)
+    optin = prov.get("allow_insecure_endpoint")
+    models = prov.get("models") or {}
+    return {
+        "name": name,
+        "type": prov.get("type", "openai"),
+        "endpoint": prov.get("endpoint") or "",
+        "keyless": prov.get("keyless") is True,
+        "allow_insecure_endpoint": canonical_optin_host(optin, name) if optin is not None else None,
+        "auth_env": auth_env,
+        "cli": _is_cli_provider(prov),
+        "models": sorted(models.keys()) if isinstance(models, dict) else [],
+    }
+
+
+def _main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="endpoint_policy")
+    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
+    lp = sub.add_parser("list-providers")
+    lp.add_argument("--project-root", default=None)
+    dp = sub.add_parser("describe-provider")
+    dp.add_argument("name")
+    dp.add_argument("--project-root", default=None)

+"""cycle-129 FR-7 (SDD D-7.1, D-7.2; sprint-257 Task 3.1, AC-3.1).
+
+Every example block in `.loa.config.yaml.example` marked `# @example-begin <name>` …
+`# @example-end` is uncommented, merged over the System defaults with the real cheval
+loader, and must load. The insecure-endpoint refusals (a public http host, a boolean
+opt-in, an opt-in naming a public host, a DNS name, a link-local or metadata address,
+a unique-local IPv6 address, a mismatched host) each fail at load with a named reason;
+`::1`, `[::1]` and RFC1918 opt-ins are accepted when they match; one provider's opt-in
+leaves another provider's refusals intact.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+import re
+import shutil
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Tuple
+
+import pytest
+import yaml
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
+
+from loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy import EndpointPolicyError  # noqa: E402
+from loa_cheval.config.loader import clear_config_cache, load_config  # noqa: E402
+from loa_cheval.types import ConfigError  # noqa: E402
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+EXAMPLE = REPO_ROOT / ".loa.config.yaml.example"
+DEFAULTS = REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "defaults" / "model-config.yaml"
+
+_BEGIN = re.compile(r"^#\s*@example-begin\s+([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\s*$")
+_END = re.compile(r"^#\s*@example-end\s*$")
+
+
+def extract_examples(text: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
+    """(name, uncommented YAML) for every marked block. One leading `#` and one
+    following space are removed per line; a nested or unterminated block fails."""
+    blocks: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
+    name = None
+    lines: List[str] = []
+    for raw in text.splitlines():
+        if name is None:
+            m = _BEGIN.match(raw)
+            if m:
+                name, lines = m.group(1), []
+            elif _END.match(raw):
+                raise AssertionError("@example-end without @example-begin")
+            continue
+        if _BEGIN.match(raw):
+            raise AssertionError(f"nested @example-begin inside {name}")
+        if _END.match(raw):
+            blocks.append((name, "\n".join(lines) + "\n"))
+            name = None
+            continue
+        assert raw.startswith("#"), f"example {name}: every line must be commented: {raw!r}"
+        body = raw[1:]
+        lines.append(body[1:] if body.startswith(" ") else body)
+    assert name is None, f"unterminated example block {name}"
+    return blocks
+
+
+def _project(tmp_path: Path, hounfour: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    root = tmp_path / "proj"
+    (root / ".claude" / "defaults").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    shutil.copy(DEFAULTS, root / ".claude" / "defaults" / "model-config.yaml")
+    (root / ".loa.config.yaml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump({"hounfour": hounfour}, sort_keys=False))
+    return str(root)
+
+
+def _load(tmp_path: Path, hounfour: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    clear_config_cache()
+    merged, _ = load_config(project_root=_project(tmp_path, hounfour))
+    return merged
+
+
+EXAMPLES = extract_examples(EXAMPLE.read_text())
+_BY_NAME = {n: yaml.safe_load(y)["hounfour"] for n, y in EXAMPLES}
+
+
+def test_marked_examples_are_present():
+    names = [n for n, _ in EXAMPLES]
+    assert len(names) == len(set(names)), names
+    for required in ("conservative", "budget-conscious", "azure-openai", "local-openai-compatible"):
+        assert required in names, f"example {required} is not marked in {EXAMPLE.name}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name, body", EXAMPLES, ids=[n for n, _ in EXAMPLES])
+def test_every_marked_example_loads(tmp_path, name, body):
+    doc = yaml.safe_load(body)
+    assert isinstance(doc, dict) and "hounfour" in doc, f"example {name} must be a `hounfour:` block"
+    merged = _load(tmp_path, doc["hounfour"])
+    for prov in (doc["hounfour"].get("providers") or {}):
+        assert prov in merged["providers"]
+
+
+def test_azure_example_carries_the_required_model_fields(tmp_path):
+    merged = _load(tmp_path, _BY_NAME["azure-openai"])
+    model = merged["providers"]["azure-openai"]["models"]["gpt-5-azure"]
+    for key in ("endpoint_family", "auth_type", "dispatch_group", "context_window", "max_output_tokens"):

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.3 (PRD FR-7 AC-7.5, SDD D-7.4, D-7.6).
+#
+# The dissent budget pre-check prices every planned voice — the primary, the companion's first hop, each advisory voice —
+# at its catalog price (python3 -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias), instead of the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok.
+# An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 for that voice and is said by name; a zero-priced entry estimates
+# zero and is said too. Prices come from fixture entries in the test's project config (hounfour.providers overlays the
+# catalog, as cheval merges it). Each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 × output rate, micro-USD/Mtok → cents.
+# =============================================================================
+
+load adversarial-review-s3-helpers
+
+setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3bud; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
+teardown() { s3_teardown; }
+
+_cfg() {  # <model> <budget> <companion_voice> [extra code_review lines]
+    s3_config "hounfour:
+  providers:
+    openai:
+      models:
+        fixture-priced:
+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 2000000, output_per_mtok: 8000000}
+    fixturelocal:
+      models:
+        fixture-zero:
+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0}
+        fixture-stale:
+          price_date: \"2000-01-01\"
+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 1000000, output_per_mtok: 1000000}
+flatline_protocol:
+  code_review:
+    enabled: true
+    model: $1
+    budget_cents: $2
+    timeout_seconds: 30
+    companion_voice: $3
+    fallback_chain: []
+${4:-}"
+}
+
+_big_diff() {  # a diff whose estimate is 1,000,500 input tokens (3,000,000 bytes / 3 + 500)
+    { printf 'diff --git a/x.sh b/x.sh\n'; head -c $(( 3000000 - 25 )) /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a'; } > "$T/diff.patch"
+    [ "$(wc -c < "$T/diff.patch")" -eq 3000000 ]
+}
+
+@test "BUD-1 the primary is priced at its catalog rate (no fixed-rate fallback): 1,000,500 tokens × 2 + 2000 × 8 USD/Mtok = 201c" {
+    _big_diff
+    _cfg fixture-priced 150 false
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.status' <<<"$result")" = "budget_exceeded" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "201" ]
+    [ "$(jq -c '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | {role, alias, estimated_cents, pricing_source}]' <<<"$result")" = '[{"role":"primary","alias":"fixture-priced","estimated_cents":201,"pricing_source":"config"}]' ]
+    grep -qF "budget: estimate 201c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-priced 201c)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    ! grep -q "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "a catalog-priced primary fell back"; return 1; }
+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
+}
+
+@test "BUD-2 an alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok for that voice, said by name (1000c + 6c)" {
+    _big_diff
+    _cfg mystery-model-x 150 false
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.estimate_voices[0].pricing_source' <<<"$result")" = "fallback" ]
+    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (primary) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice" "$T/stderr.log"
+    [ "$(grep -c "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log")" = "1" ]
+}
+
+@test "BUD-3 a zero-priced entry estimates 0c and is said: a 0-cent budget admits it, where the fixed rate would refuse" {
+    _cfg fixture-zero 0 false
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (primary) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -qF "budget: estimate 0c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-zero 0c)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -qx "fixture-zero" "$CALLS"
+    # the same run priced at the fixed rate is refused (the regression this replaces: 2000 output tokens × 30 = 6c > 0)
+    _cfg mystery-model-x 0 false
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
